# Feature: Atlas Follow-up — WebGL Tool Registry (#750)

<!-- auto-generated by /implement — Closes #750 -->

## Intent

Native WebGL toolbar derives allowed tools from `ATLAS_TOOL_REGISTRY` (same semantic allow-list as 2D). Hardcoded prototype tool arrays are not product authority. Illegal kind-tool pairs and unauthorized commits are rejected client-side; RPC/RLS remain the authorization boundary.

## Preconditions

- Domain registry from #720 (`atlasToolsForKind` / `createsCanonicalNode: false`).
- Product WebGL host `AtlasNative3dEditor` + controlled mount (#721/#747).
- Bidirectional 2D/3D shared document (#749).

## Happy Path

- [x] `webglToolChromeForKind` builds WebGL chrome from `ATLAS_TOOL_REGISTRY` (brush→paint runtime id)
- [x] Runtime `#tools` uses registry chrome when provided (`data-atlas-tool-source=registry`); demo fallback only without chrome
- [x] Country tip → Gelände + Weg/Grenze (road disabled in 3D with reason); building tip → Wand/Raum/Stempel, not continent brush
- [x] Kind change resets illegal active tool to `hand`
- [x] `assertWebglToolCommit` / runtime `allowMutation` reject unauthorized or illegal tools
- [x] `AtlasNative3dEditor` receives `activeNodeKind` + `canEdit` from `UnifiedAtlasEditor`
- [x] Check + composition CLEAR

## Edge Cases

- Unsupported registry tools (`select`, `road`) remain visible but disabled with DE reason
- `canEdit=false` blocks paint/stamp/wall/room/erase mutations; hand/nav still works
- Stamps never set `createsCanonicalNode`

## Security Coverage

- Client gate is UX only; map upsert / world-node RPCs stay owner-scoped (RLS)
- F-03: hidden toolbar buttons are not an authorization boundary

## Scope

**In:** registry→WebGL chrome, kind/permission gating, check/evidence  
**Out:** new 3D brush assets; treating stamps as WorldNode creates; full road/select 3D drawing
